title: Indian Court Supports OpenAI: Using News Content to Train AI Is Not Infringing; Case May Set Global Trend

content_html:
OpenAI has won a landmark legal victory in India. On July 24 local time, the Delhi High Court ruled that OpenAI's use of content from Asian International News Agency (ANI) to train its artificial intelligence model does not constitute copyright infringement. This ruling not only clears legal obstacles for OpenAI in India, but could also provide important judicial references for global copyright disputes over AI training data.

"Fair use" withstands the copyright crackdown, public interest overrides the injunction request

Judge Amit Bansal clearly stated in the judgment that OpenAI's actions fall under the "fair use" exception defined in India's Copyright Act. At the same time, ANI failed to submit sufficient evidence to the court proving direct copying of ANI's copyrighted content in ChatGPT's responses. These two core findings fundamentally undermine ANI's legal basis.

More notably, the judge carefully weighed the consequences of the injunction. The judgment emphasized that issuing any temporary injunction at this stage would be detrimental to the overall development of artificial intelligence, especially affecting large language model projects currently being developed in India. The judge further pointed out that if the injunction were implemented, it would have widespread negative impacts on the public interest - a large number of users in India who freely use ChatGPT would be the first to suffer. On the scale between technological innovation and copyright protection, the Delhi High Court clearly placed the weight on the former.

The timing of this ruling is rather delicate. Just as news publishers around the world are collectively pressuring AI companies to pay for training data, this ruling from the Indian court provides rare and strong legal support for the AI industry. Previously, media outlets such as The New York Times have filed similar lawsuits against OpenAI in the United States, and the case is still under review. Whether the ruling from the Delhi High Court will serve as a reference for judges in other jurisdictions will become an important signal to closely monitor in the global AI copyright dispute in the coming period.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 在印度赢得了具有里程碑意义的法律胜利。 当地时间7月24日，德里高等法院裁定OpenAI使用亚洲国际通讯社（ANI）的内容来训练其人工智能模型的行为不构成版权侵权。 该裁决不仅为OpenAI在印度扫清了法律障碍，也可为全球人工智能训练数据版权纠纷提供重要的司法参考。

“合理使用”经受住版权打压，公共利益凌驾于禁令请求之上

法官 Amit Bansal 在判决中明确表示，OpenAI 的行为属于印度版权法中定义的“合理使用”例外。 同时，ANI 未能向法院提交足够的证据证明 ChatGPT 的回复中直接复制了 ANI 的版权内容。 这两项核心调查结果从根本上破坏了 ANI 的法律基础。

更值得注意的是，法官仔细权衡了禁令的后果。 判决强调，现阶段发布任何临时禁令都会不利于人工智能的整体发展，特别是影响印度目前正在开发的大型语言模型项目。 法官进一步指出，如果该禁令得以实施，将对公共利益产生广泛的负面影响——大量自由使用ChatGPT的印度用户将首当其冲。 在技​​术创新与版权保护之间的尺度上，德里高等法院显然偏重于前者。

这项裁决的时机相当微妙。 正当全球新闻出版商集体向AI公司施压，要求其支付训练数据费用时，印度法院的这一裁决为AI行业提供了难得的强有力的法律支持。 此前，《纽约时报》等媒体已在美国对OpenAI提起类似诉讼，目前案件仍在审理中。 德里高等法院的裁决能否为其他司法管辖区的法官提供参考，将成为未来一段时期全球人工智能版权纠纷中值得密切关注的重要信号。
